inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for the six months to 30 June 2026 (2,993m basic + 25m employee-scheme dilution), H1 2026 report EPS note. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. BAE actually repurchases more than it grants (GBP 502m bought back vs GBP 174m SBC in FY2025; GBP 247m in H1 2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention the company has yet to pay for.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Cost of equity-settled employee share schemes' GBP 174m (FY2024 GBP 144m). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; the SOCE 'Share-based payments (inclusive of tax)' GBP 226m includes a deferred-tax credit, not cash withheld, so the cash-flow add-back is the basis used.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; the LSE quote is in pence sterling (GBp, 1/100 GBP). Per-share values are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to pence. This is a definitional unit conversion, not a market FX rate, so it carries no date risk. Magnitude check: a GBP 15-20 per-share value must print as 1,500-2,000p against a 1,921p quote.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:41:38Z regular close (LSE Friday close; Yahoo had not posted a 2026-10-05 bar at build time)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, 5.0% UK equity risk premium, beta ~0.75 for a backlog-driven defence prime (cost of equity ~8.25%); pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (BBB+/Baa1 bonds), ~3.6% after 25% UK tax; ~11% debt weight at a GBP 58bn market cap gives ~7.7%, rounded up to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, customer concentration and execution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full FY2025 lease cash cost -- GBP 187m principal (financing) + GBP 79m interest on lease liabilities (note 6) = GBP 266m, 0.94% of revenue -- is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (GBP 1,766m at 30 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (GBP 1,173m - GBP 228m = GBP 945m, 3.33%) so the lease is not charged twice. This matches BAE's own 'free cash flow' (after lease principal) and 'net debt (excluding lease liabilities)' definitions.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. Flows are consolidated (statutory operating profit includes 100% of subsidiaries), so the NCI's share of value is deducted in equity_bridge at GBP 1,200m: the c.GBP 80m FY2026 guided NCI profit share (GBP 89m FY2025, GBP 85m FY2024; dividends to NCI GBP 86m, i.e. near-full payout) at 15x. The GBP 172m book value would understate it badly. No NCI leakage is folded into the tax path.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year explicit horizon, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied (GBP WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule). BAE is a backlog-driven defence prime (GBP 84.0bn order book at H1 2026, ~2.7x revenue), 96% government revenue, four governments = 73% of revenue. EBITDA BASIS: the engine's ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC and PRE-LEASE-COST: statutory operating profit GBP 2,925m + D&A GBP 1,173m + SBC GBP 174m = GBP 4,272m, 15.08% of IFRS revenue GBP 28,336m (the CSV's EBITDA of GBP 4,098m is post-SBC). The equity-accounted share of results (GBP 194m, mainly MBDA) is INSIDE statutory operating profit and hence inside the flows, so the GBP 614m EAI book value is NOT added in the bridge (matching-asset rule); the EAI profit share is taxed at the group cash rate in the build although it is already post-tax -- a small conservatism. REVENUE BASIS: IFRS revenue (GBP 28,336m), not the company's 'Sales' (GBP 30,662m, which adds the proportional share of EAI sales); FY2026 guidance (+8-10% sales, constant currency at $1.32) is applied to the IFRS line. PENSION: net IAS 19 surplus GBP 1,075m at 30 Jun 2026 (GBP 1,478m surplus asset less GBP 403m obligations) is NOT added to the bridge -- a UK pension surplus is trustee-controlled and a refund bears 35% withholding tax; deficit-recovery contributions have ended (FY2024 contributions exceeded the charge by GBP 249m, FY2025 by GBP 50m, H1 2026 by GBP 5m), so the forward flows carry no deficit drag. This is a deliberate conservatism worth roughly 20-25p/share if ever accessed. CAPEX: gross PPE + intangibles GBP 1,103m (3.9%); GBP 122m of customer 'proceeds from funding related to assets' is NOT credited against it (conservative). WORKING CAPITAL: BAE's reported FCF swings with customer advances (FY2024 +GBP 745m, FY2025 -GBP 345m, H1 2026 strongly positive); base capture is 0% of the revenue change, bear -5% (advances unwind as growth slows), bull +3%. CASH TAX: GBP 196m paid in FY2025 (~7% of model EBIT) and GBP 175m in FY2024 against a c.22% guided underlying ETR, reflecting R&D expenditure credits, US R&D expensing and pension deductions; the cash rate is ramped to 22% by year 5 rather than perpetuating the shelter. NET DEBT: borrowings GBP 7,387m (GBP 6,686m non-current + GBP 701m current) less cash GBP 4,200m = GBP 3,187m at 30 Jun 2026; the company's KPI 'net debt (excluding lease liabilities)' is GBP 3,173m (nets small derivative/collateral items). BAE's own FCF (GBP 2,158m FY2025, >GBP 2.0bn FY2026 guidance) is LEVERED (after GBP 433m net interest paid and lease principal, including GBP 299m EAI dividends); reported_fcf here is the CSV's OCF less capex GBP 2,329m, which is pre-interest and pre-lease, so the component build (which charges leases but not interest) sits between the two definitions. PRICE: Friday 2026-10-02 regular close; replace at the next regular close.
inputs.fcf_definitions_note: Company FCF FY2025 GBP 2,158m = OCF 3,432 + EAI dividends 299 - net interest paid 433 - net capex & financial investment 953 - lease principal 187 (FY2025 AR APM reconciliation). CSV FCF GBP 2,329m = OCF 3,432 - gross capex 1,103.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at value (c.GBP 80m FY2026 guided NCI profit share x 15x)
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 guidance 'Non-controlling interests c.GBP 80m'; FY2025 NCI share GBP 89m, dividends paid to NCI GBP 86m. Book value GBP 172m at 30 Jun 2026 would understate the claim. Charged here and nowhere else.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (sales +8-10% constant currency, upgraded at H1 2026 from +7-9%), applied as year-1 growth and decelerated toward terminal growth; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are unusable as a growth anchor: the 5-year figure (20.5%) is inflated by the FY2020 pension-deficit trough (equity GBP 4.6bn) unwinding into an IAS 19 surplus (GBP 11.2bn by FY2022), and the 3-year figure (1.7%) is depressed by GBP 1.9bn of buybacks and GBP 2.8bn of dividends on a GBP 11bn base. Revenue (10.1%/8.0%) and EPS (10.4%/10.9%) agree with each other and with guidance; they are the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (CSV OCF-less-capex FCF minus SBC; interest received sits in investing, not OCF, so no interest adjustment is needed on this series). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR 1.8% vs reported 2.8%: SBC grew from GBP 101m to GBP 174m (14.6%/yr) against FCF growing 2.8%/yr, so a rising share of reported FCF growth is paid in stock. Both 5-year FCF CAGRs start from the FY2020 Covid/pension-contribution trough (FCF GBP 689m) and overstate trend growth; FY2022-FY2025 FCF was flat at GBP 2.1-2.8bn because capex doubled (GBP 693m to GBP 1,103m) while OCF grew 21%.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = midpoint of upgraded FY2026 sales guidance (+8-10%). FY2027-28 at 7%/6% is the backlog converting (GBP 84bn book, 2.7x revenue; Dreadnought GBP 5.9bn, GCAP/Edgewing >GBP 5bn, Turkiye Typhoon, THAAD seekers, munitions ramps) with order intake growth decelerating off the base. Fades to 2.5% nominal by year 10 as allied budgets settle near the NATO 3.5%-of-GDP path.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 pre-SBC EBITDA 15.08%. Guidance has EBIT growing ~2pp faster than sales, i.e. ~20bp/yr of return-on-sales expansion from Maritime (6.7% RoS) maturing and US munitions/space capacity filling; the path adds ~10bp/yr to 15.6% and then holds, below the Electronic Systems/Air sector margins so the mix drag from Maritime is retained.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax paid was ~7% of model EBIT in FY2025 and FY2024 against a c.22% guided underlying ETR. Ramped 12% -> 22% over five years; perpetuating the R&D-credit/US-expensing shelter would be the 'perpetuated tax shelter' error.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 gross capex 3.9% of revenue, roughly double the FY2016-21 run-rate (~2.5%) as munitions, Barrow and US capacity are built. Tapers to 3.4%, slightly above D&A ex-ROU (3.3%), consistent with a business still growing 2.5-3% nominal.

scenario_narratives.base: The GBP 84bn backlog converts on schedule: FY2026 lands at the midpoint of the upgraded guidance (+9% sales, +11% EBIT, >GBP 2.0bn FCF), then growth decelerates through 7%/6%/5% as order intake flattens off a record base while Dreadnought, SSN-AUKUS, GCAP, Type 26 exports and US munitions/space capacity sustain mid-single-digit growth into the 2030s. Return on sales widens ~10-20bp/yr as Maritime matures from 6.7% and US capacity fills, reaching a 15.6% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Cash tax normalises to the 22% guided rate by 2030 as R&D-credit and US expensing timing benefits unwind. Capex steps down from 3.9% to 3.4% of revenue once the munitions and shipyard builds complete. Customer advances net to zero over the horizon.
scenario_narratives.bull: Allied budgets track the NATO 3.5%-of-GDP pledge, the UK Strategic Defence Review funds the shipyard/reactor expansion and GCAP in full, Turkiye/Saudi/Canada/Norway exports land on time and the US segments (Electronic Systems ~15% RoS, Space & Mission Systems) grow faster than the group. Sales compound 10%/9%/8% through FY2028 and the mix shift toward US electronics and sustainment lifts the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 16.8%. Cash tax stays below the headline rate for longer (21% terminal) as US R&D expensing persists, capex normalises to 3.3%, and advances remain a modest tailwind (+3% capture). Terminal growth 2.75% reflects a structurally larger defence share of GDP.
scenario_narratives.bear: Geopolitical de-escalation (a Ukraine settlement, a quieter Middle East) removes the urgency from budget growth after FY2026; UK fiscal consolidation and US continuing resolutions delay awards, and order intake drops below 1x book-to-bill. Growth fades to 1-2% from FY2028. Fixed-price overruns on early-stage Maritime and GCAP work and under-absorbed new munitions capacity compress the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 13.6%; advances unwind (-5% capture) so FCF trails earnings; capex stays at 3.5% to finish committed facilities; cash tax normalises faster (23%) as US credits lapse. The terminal multiple is capped at 15x -- the market's pre-2022 view of the stock (sub-13x P/E), when defence was a low-growth annuity rather than a growth sector. No going-concern element: the balance sheet is investment-grade and the GBP 84bn backlog funds the decade either way.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the house 15/50/35 default to 20/50/30. Bear up to 20%: the bear case is not solvency (investment-grade, GBP 84bn backlog) but a plausible single macro switch -- de-escalation removing the budget tailwind -- combined with fixed-price execution risk on early-stage Maritime/GCAP work, and 73% customer concentration in four governments means one budget decision moves a quarter of revenue. Bull down to 30%: it needs three independent things to hold simultaneously (budgets reaching 3.5% of GDP, export wins landing on time, and the US mix delivering a 1.7pp margin expansion that BAE has never achieved in a decade of 14.4-15.9% EBITDA margins). Base 50% is the guided path, which management has met or beaten in every half since FY2022.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BAE is valued as a long-duration, government-funded annuity with a visible decade of backlog conversion: a 10-year owner-FCF build at an 8% GBP WACC, SBC expensed and the share count held flat, leases charged as an operating cost, the NCI deducted at value, cash tax ramped to the guided 22%, and the pension surplus and customer-funded capex deliberately left uncredited. The result is deliberately a 'what the cash flows are worth' number, not a re-rating thesis: the stock's move from sub-13x to 20x+ earnings since 2022 is the market pre-paying for the budget upcycle, and the gap between the house value and the price is the price of that thesis, stated explicitly.
key_risks_to_valuation: Budget cycle reversal: de-escalation in Ukraine or the Middle East removes the growth premium; the bear case (1-2% growth from FY2028) is the valuation's biggest swing factor
Customer concentration: four governments = 73% of revenue; a single US continuing resolution, UK spending review or Saudi programme pause is material
Fixed-price execution on early-stage Maritime (6.7% RoS), GCAP and new munitions capacity; a 1pp margin miss is worth ~GBP 300m of EBITDA
FX: a 5c move in GBP/USD is ~GBP 500m of sales and ~GBP 70m of EBIT; guidance is at $1.32
Cash tax normalisation: the model ramps from ~7% paid to 22%; if the R&D/US-expensing shelter persists the house value is conservative, if the ramp is faster it is generous by ~1 year of tax
Terminal assumptions: ~60% of value sits in the terminal; the 18x cap binds in base and bull, so a lower exit multiple (the bear's 15x) is the second-largest sensitivity after growth
Regulatory/ESG: the Aug-2026 $36m ITAR settlement and ongoing scrutiny of Saudi sales are headline rather than cash risks, but a sanctions event on a major customer would not be
